en: to move emotionally; to touch; to impress

examples.en: That song moved everyone.
I want to move my parents with a letter.
It is a film that moves people.
A small gift touches a friend.
What touched the teacher was the student's effort.

examples.ko: 말만으로는 그 사람을 감동시킬 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't move that person with words alone.

explain: 느끼게 하는 쪽이 주어예요. 느끼는 사람이 주어이면 '감동받다'를 써요. '노래가 나를 감동시켰어요'와 '나는 노래에 감동받았어요'를 비교해 보세요.

phrases.example: 그 영화는 저에게 큰 감동을 줬어요.
phrases.en: That movie moved me deeply.
phrases.nuance_ko: '감동시키다'와 뜻이 비슷하고 더 자연스럽게 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '감동시키다' and often sounds more natural.

phrases.en: I was moved after reading my friend's letter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 느끼는 사람이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when the person who feels the emotion is the subject.

explain_en: The subject is whoever causes the feeling. If the person who feels it is the subject, use '감동받다'. Compare '노래가 나를 감동시켰어요' with '나는 노래에 감동받았어요'.

en: to show around; to let someone see

examples.en: I showed my friend around Seoul.
I want to take my child to see the zoo.

examples.ko: 외국 친구에게 부산을 구경시켜서 하루가 금방 갔어요.
examples.en: I showed my foreign friend around Busan, and the day flew by.
It is time to show the guests around the factory.
Next time, there are many places I can show you.
I showed my family around my office and they all liked it.

explain: '구경하다'는 내가 보는 것이고 '구경시키다'는 다른 사람이 볼 수 있게 해 주는 거예요. 보통 '구경시켜 주다', '구경시켜 드리다'로 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '보여 주다'도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I showed my younger sibling around our school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 가족처럼 편한 사람에게 보여 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when showing someone around, such as friends or family.

phrases.en: I showed my parents my room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람에게 보여 줄 때는 '드리다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 드리다 when the person is older or higher in status.

phrases.en: I showed my friend our house.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구경시키다'보다 짧고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter than 구경시키다 and more common in everyday talk.

explain_en: 구경하다 is when you look around yourself, while 구경시키다 is letting someone else look around. It usually appears as 구경시켜 주다 or 구경시켜 드리다. 보여 주다 is also a common alternative.

en: to make remember; to make recall

examples.en: The teacher made a song to help us remember the words.
This ad makes you remember the brand name.
I got my child to memorize our home address.

examples.ko: 부모님은 어릴 때부터 제 이름과 전화번호를 기억시키셨어요.
examples.en: My parents made me remember my name and phone number from when I was little.
We need to make the staff remember the safety rules.

examples.ko: 시험 날짜를 학생들에게 기억시키는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It is good to make students remember the exam date.

explain: 다른 사람이 기억하게 만든다는 말이에요. 비슷한 상황에서 한국 사람들은 '알려 주다', '상기시키다', '외우게 하다'도 써요. '기억하다'가 내가 기억하는 것이라면 이 말은 상대를 향해요.

phrases.en: I help people remember words with a song.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기억시키다'보다 일상에서 더 자연스럽고 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more natural in daily speech than '기억시키다'.

phrases.en: I said my name many times so they'd remember it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목적을 나타내는 연결형으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common connecting form for stating a purpose.

phrases.example: 저는 사람들에게 제 이름을 기억시키지 못했어요.
phrases.en: I couldn't make people remember my name.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 기억하게 하는 데 실패했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you failed to make others remember.

explain_en: It means causing another person to remember something. In similar situations Koreans also use '알려 주다' (let someone know), '상기시키다' (remind) and '외우게 하다' (make someone memorize). '기억하다' is what you do yourself, while 기억시키다 is directed at someone else.

en: to frighten; to scare; to shock

examples.ko: 생일에 몰래 준비해서 엄마를 놀래 줬어요.
examples.en: I secretly prepared something on her birthday and surprised my mom.
Do not startle the child with a loud voice.
I am going to surprise my husband with a surprise party.

examples.ko: 뒤에서 갑자기 소리를 질러서 저를 놀랬어요.
examples.en: He suddenly shouted from behind and startled me.
I did not mean to scare you, sorry.
I even scared my younger sibling with a scary mask.

explain: '놀라다'는 내가 놀라는 것이고, '놀래다'는 다른 사람을 놀라게 하는 것이에요: '친구를 놀래다'. 내가 놀랐을 때는 '놀랐어요'예요. 입말에서 '놀래키다'라고도 하지만 표준어는 '놀래다'예요.

phrases.example: 남편을 놀래 주고 싶어서 케이크를 준비했어요.
phrases.en: I wanted to surprise my husband, so I prepared a cake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깜짝 선물처럼 즐겁게 놀라게 하고 싶을 때 쓰는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used when you want to surprise someone in a fun way.

phrases.example: 큰 소리로 사람을 놀라게 하지 마세요.
phrases.en: Please don't startle people with a loud noise.
phrases.nuance_ko: '놀래다'와 뜻이 같고, 더 널리 쓰이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 놀래다, and more widely used.

phrases.example: 숨어 있다가 친구를 깜짝 놀래 줬어요.
phrases.en: I hid and then gave my friend a big scare.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깜짝'을 붙이면 갑자기 놀라게 한다는 느낌이 더 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 깜짝 stresses the sudden surprise.

explain_en: '놀라다' is when you are startled yourself; 'nollaeda' is when you startle someone else, as in '친구를 놀래다'. When you are the one startled, say '놀랐어요'. In speech you may hear '놀래키다', but the standard word is '놀래다'.

examples.ko: 유아 전용 놀이방이 있는 식당이라 아기 손님이 많이 와요.
examples.en: It's a restaurant with a play room for little kids, so many baby customers come.
I leave my child at the daycare and go to work.
At the daycare, he plays with blocks with his friends.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 놀이방은 오후 일곱 시까지 열어요.
examples.en: The daycare in our neighborhood is open until seven in the evening.

examples.ko: 놀이방 선생님이 아이를 잘 돌봐 주세요.
examples.en: The daycare teacher takes good care of the child.

examples.ko: 거실 한쪽에 아이 놀이방을 따로 만들었어요.
examples.en: We made a separate play room for the child in one corner of the living room.

explain: 아이를 돌봐 주는 시설을 말하기도 하고, 식당이나 집 안에 아이가 놀 수 있게 만든 공간을 말하기도 해요. 시설을 말할 때는 요즘 보통 '어린이집'이라고 불러요. 뜻이 두 가지라서 문장에서 시설인지 공간인지 구분해서 읽어요.

phrases.en: My child goes to daycare.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시설을 말할 때 요즘 더 흔하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The more common word these days for the childcare facility.

phrases.en: I leave my child at the daycare while I work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이를 돌봐 주는 시설이라는 뜻으로 쓸 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits when you mean the facility that looks after children.
phrases.en_equiv: to leave a child at daycare

phrases.en: It's convenient to go to a restaurant that has a play area.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이때는 시설이 아니라 아이가 노는 공간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Here it means a play space, not a childcare facility.

explain_en: It can mean a facility that looks after children, or a space in a restaurant or home made for kids to play. For the facility, people now usually call it '어린이집'. Since it has two meanings, check from the sentence whether it is a facility or a space.

examples.en: The mother lays her sleeping baby on the bed.
The nurse carefully laid the patient on the bed.

examples.ko: 아이를 바닥에 누이고 이불을 덮어 줬어요.
examples.en: I laid the child on the floor and covered him with a blanket.

examples.ko: 피곤한 동생을 소파에 누여서 쉬게 했어요.
examples.en: I laid my tired younger sibling on the sofa to rest.

examples.ko: 아기를 바르게 누일 때는 머리를 받쳐 주세요.
examples.en: When you lay a baby down, please support the head.

examples.ko: 할머니를 방에 누인 뒤에 물을 가져왔어요.
examples.en: After laying my grandmother down in the room, I brought water.

explain: '눕다'는 내가 눕는 것이고, '누이다'는 다른 사람을 눕게 하는 것이에요. 아기나 환자처럼 스스로 눕기 힘든 사람에게 써요. 비슷한 말로 '눕히다'가 있어요.

phrases.en: Dad lays the baby on the bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 같고 일상에서 '누이다'보다 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, and more common in daily speech than 누이다.

phrases.en: Please lay the sick friend down on the sofa.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람을 도와서 눕게 해 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when helping someone lie down.

phrases.en: I laid the baby down and covered her with a blanket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눕힌 다음에 이어지는 행동을 말할 때 연결해서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links the laying down to the next action.

explain_en: '눕다' is when you lie down yourself; 'nuida' is when you lay someone else down, such as a baby or a patient who cannot lie down alone. A similar word is '눕히다'.

examples.en: I give the baby a bath every evening.
I gave our puppy a bath on the weekend.

examples.ko: 아이를 목욕시킨 뒤에 로션을 발라 줬어요.
examples.en: After bathing the child, I put lotion on him.
Please bathe the baby with warm water.
Today I will give my younger sibling a bath.
After the bath, the child falls asleep right away.

explain: '목욕하다'는 내가 씻는 것이고, '목욕시키다'는 아기나 반려동물처럼 다른 대상을 씻기는 것이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '씻기다'도 써요.

phrases.en: I give my little sibling a bath on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람을 도와서 씻겨 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when helping someone else bathe.

phrases.en: Mom washes the baby with warm water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻이고, 일상에서 더 짧게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, a shorter everyday word.

phrases.en: I bathed the puppy and dried its fur.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목욕시킨 다음에 이어지는 일을 말할 때 연결해서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links the bath to the next action.

explain_en: '목욕하다' is bathing yourself; 'mogyoksikida' is bathing someone else, such as a baby or a pet. '씻기다' is used in the same way.

examples.ko: 감기 기운이 있을 때 생강차를 마셔요.
examples.en: I drink ginger tea when I feel like I'm catching a cold.
One cup of warm ginger tea, please.

examples.ko: 생강차는 꿀을 넣으면 맛이 더 부드러워요.
examples.en: Ginger tea tastes smoother if you add honey.
I warmed myself up with ginger tea on a cold day.
In winter, citron tea is good and ginger tea is good too.
This café is famous for its tasty ginger tea.

explain: '차'가 붙었지만 찻잎이 아니라 생강을 끓이거나 우려서 만든 음료예요. 한국에서는 '유자차, 대추차, 쌍화차'처럼 이런 전통차가 많아요. 감기에 걸렸을 때나 몸이 찰 때 찾는 사람이 많아요.

phrases.en: I had a cold, so I boiled ginger tea at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생강을 넣고 직접 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you make it yourself with ginger.

phrases.en: If you add honey to ginger tea, it's less spicy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맛이 맵기 때문에 꿀을 같이 넣는 경우가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Ginger tea is spicy, so people often add honey.
phrases.en_equiv: to put honey in ginger tea

phrases.example: 생강차가 너무 매워서 다 못 마셨어요.
phrases.en: The ginger tea was so spicy that I couldn't drink it all.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생강 맛이 강할 때 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when the ginger flavor is strong.

explain_en: Although it ends in '차', it is not made from tea leaves but from ginger that is boiled or steeped. Korea has many traditional drinks like this, such as '유자차', '대추차' and '쌍화차'. Many people reach for it when they have a cold or feel chilly.

examples.en: After dinner I walked to help my food settle.
I took the stairs to help digest my food.

examples.ko: 위가 음식을 소화시키는 데 시간이 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes time for the stomach to digest food.
I'm full, so I'll let it settle before I work out.

examples.ko: 아기가 우유를 소화시키지 못해서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: The baby couldn't digest milk, so we went to the hospital.
I drink coffee after my lunch has settled.

explain: '소화되다'는 음식이 저절로 소화되는 것이고, '소화시키다'는 사람이나 몸이 소화되게 만드는 것이에요. 산책이나 운동처럼 일부러 하는 행동 뒤에 자연스럽게 나와요.

phrases.en: After dinner I help my digestion with a walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소화시키다'와 같은 뜻이고, 말할 때 '소화를 시키다'도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '소화시키다'; '소화를 시키다' is also common in speech.

phrases.en: Warm tea helps digestion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이나 행동이 소화에 좋을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when a food or action is good for digestion.

phrases.en: Light food is digested quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소화시키다'는 사람이 소화되게 하는 것이고, '소화되다'는 음식이 저절로 소화되는 것이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '소화시키다' means a person makes digestion happen; '소화되다' means food digests on its own.

explain_en: 소화되다 means food gets digested on its own, while 소화시키다 means a person or body makes it digest. It fits naturally after deliberate actions like a walk or exercise.

examples.en: Hydrogen is the most common element in the universe.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 물을 수소와 산소로 나누는 실험을 봤어요.
examples.en: In science class I watched an experiment splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen.

examples.ko: 수소로 달리는 버스가 우리 동네에도 생겼어요.
examples.en: A hydrogen-powered bus has started running in our neighborhood too.

examples.ko: 수소를 채운 풍선은 하늘로 높이 떠올라요.
examples.en: A balloon filled with hydrogen floats high into the sky.

examples.ko: 물 분자에는 수소 원자 두 개와 산소 원자 한 개가 들어 있어요.
examples.en: A water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

examples.ko: 수소 충전소가 어디에 있는지 지도 앱으로 찾아봤어요.
examples.en: I looked up on a map app where the hydrogen charging station is.

explain: 원소 이름에는 '수소', '산소', '질소', '탄소'처럼 '-소'로 끝나는 것이 많아요. '수소차', '수소 에너지'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여 새 말을 자주 만들어요.

phrases.en: A hydrogen car gives off water instead of smoke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수소로 움직이는 자동차예요. '수소'에 '차'를 붙인 새 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A car powered by hydrogen; a compound of 수소 and 차.

phrases.en: They say hydrogen energy is good for the environment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수소로 만든 에너지를 말해요. 뉴스와 과학 이야기에서 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Energy made from hydrogen; often heard in news and science talk.

phrases.en: They put hydrogen gas inside the balloon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기체 상태의 수소를 말할 때 써요. 실험이나 산업 이야기에서 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for hydrogen in gas form, appearing in experiments and industry talk.

explain_en: Many element names end in '-소', like '수소', '산소', '질소', and '탄소'. '수소' often forms compounds such as '수소차' (hydrogen car) and '수소 에너지' (hydrogen energy).

examples.en: The top and pants go well together.
Take off your top and hang it on the chair.
The top is too small, so I should buy a new one.
Dark colors are comfortable for tops.
I put the key in my top's pocket.
It rained and my top got stained.

explain: '윗도리'와 거의 같은 뜻으로, 바지나 치마와 짝으로 말해요. '윗옷을 입다/벗다'처럼 써요. [위돋]으로 발음해요.

phrases.en: Bring one more top with you.
phrases.nuance_ko: '윗옷'과 거의 같고, 편한 대화에서 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 윗옷, natural in casual conversation.

phrases.en: I bought the top and bottom separately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷가게에서 '하의'와 짝으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with 하의 in clothing stores.

phrases.en: It's cold, so please put on a top.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 입을 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for putting on a top.

explain_en: It means almost the same as '윗도리' and is paired with pants or skirts. You say '윗옷을 입다/벗다'. It is pronounced [위돋].

en: to make someone understand; to make someone comprehend

examples.en: It's hard to make a young child understand the rules.

examples.ko: 저는 부모님을 이해시켜서 유학을 가고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to get my parents to understand and go study abroad.
I even drew a picture to make my friend understand.
Can I make them understand my position?

examples.ko: 한 시간 동안 설명해서 겨우 이해시켰어요.
examples.en: After explaining for an hour, I barely got them to understand.
Getting adults to understand is the hardest part.

explain: 상대가 알아듣도록 설명해서 받아들이게 만들 때 써요. '설득하다'와 달라서, 이해시키는 것은 알게 하는 것이고 설득하는 것은 생각이나 행동을 바꾸게 하는 것이에요. 설명하는 사람이 노력해야 한다는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 선생님이 어려운 문법을 쉽게 이해시켜 줬어요.
phrases.en: The teacher helped me understand the hard grammar easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 주다'를 붙여 누군가를 위해 이해하게 해 준다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-아/어 주다', it means making someone understand for their benefit.

phrases.en: I tried to make my friend understand how I feel.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)려고'를 붙여 이해하게 만들려는 노력을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-(으)려고', it expresses trying to make someone understand.
phrases.en_equiv: to try to make someone understand

phrases.en: I explained it simply so my younger sibling could follow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷한 말로, 일상 대화에서 더 쉽게 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar expression that's easier to use in everyday talk.
phrases.en_equiv: to explain so someone can follow

explain_en: Use it when you explain so that the other person grasps something. It differs from '설득하다': '이해시키다' is getting someone to understand, while '설득하다' is getting them to change their mind or action. It carries a feel that the explainer has to put in effort.

en: to make someone perceive; to make someone aware of

examples.en: Ads make people aware of a new product.
I made students realize how serious the problem is.
I put up a poster to raise awareness of safety.
After making him realize his mistake, I received an apology.
You need to make the child aware of the rules.
If you repeat it to make them aware, people remember.

explain: 상대가 어떤 사실을 분명히 알게 만들 때 써요. 스스로 알게 되는 것은 '인식하다', 남이 알게 하는 것은 '인식시키다'예요. 말하기에서는 '알려 주다'나 '깨닫게 하다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 사람들이 그 사실을 알게 해야 해요.
phrases.en: We have to make people aware of that fact.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인식시키다'보다 쉽고 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more natural in speech than '인식시키다'.

phrases.example: 그 사건이 안전의 중요성을 깨닫게 했어요.
phrases.en: That incident made us realize the importance of safety.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몰랐던 것을 마음으로 알게 만든다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests making someone truly realize something they hadn't understood.

phrases.en: Please make the child aware of how important the rules are.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 주다'를 붙여 부탁하거나 도와주는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 주다' gives a feeling of doing it for someone or requesting it.

explain_en: It is used when you make someone clearly aware of a fact. Becoming aware by yourself is '인식하다', and making others aware is '인식시키다'. In speech, '알려 주다' or '깨닫게 하다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: My parents enrolled me in a good school.
I am getting ready to enroll my child in elementary school.
I plan to enroll my daughter in kindergarten this year.
I felt relieved after getting my youngest enrolled.
I sent my child off to school, and the house got quiet.

examples.ko: 아들을 입학시키면 학부모 모임에 가야 해요.
examples.en: Once you enroll your son, you have to attend parents' meetings.

explain: '입학하다'는 학생이 학교에 들어가는 것이고 '입학시키다'는 부모나 보호자가 아이를 들어가게 하는 거예요. 그래서 주어가 부모예요. 학생이 주어일 때는 '입학했어요'라고 해요. 말할 때는 '학교에 보내다'를 더 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I'm going to enroll my son in elementary school next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 할 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about a future plan.

phrases.en: I sent my child to school.
phrases.nuance_ko: '입학시키다'보다 말할 때 더 자주 쓰는 편한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual and common spoken alternative to 입학시키다.

phrases.en: I want to enroll my child in a good school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부모의 바람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express a parent's wish.

explain_en: 입학하다 is when a student enters a school, while 입학시키다 is when a parent or guardian gets the child enrolled, so the subject is the parent. When the student is the subject, say 입학했어요. In speech, 학교에 보내다 is used more often.

en: to bring to a stop; to suspend

examples.en: The driver brought the bus to a stop.

examples.ko: 문제가 생기면 기계를 바로 정지시켜야 해요.
examples.en: If a problem occurs, you must stop the machine right away.

examples.ko: 회사는 규칙을 어긴 계정을 정지시키려고 해요.
examples.en: The company plans to suspend accounts that broke the rules.
You can pause the video and ask a question.

examples.ko: 비상 버튼을 누르면 열차를 정지시킬 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can stop the train by pressing the emergency button.
Please explain the reason for shutting down the factory.

explain: '정지되다'는 멈춰진 결과이고, '정지시키다'는 사람이 멈추게 하는 동작이에요. 기계, 차, 계정처럼 누군가 통제하는 대상에 써요. 일상에서 영상을 멈출 때는 '멈추다'나 '일시 정지하다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: The police made the car stop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier phrase for everyday conversation.

phrases.en: There is a problem, so please stop the machine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계를 멈춰 달라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone to stop a machine.

phrases.en: The company suspended the hacked account.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서비스나 계정을 쓰지 못하게 할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when making a service or account unusable.

explain_en: 정지되다 describes something that has been stopped, while 정지시키다 is the action of making it stop. It fits machines, vehicles or accounts that someone controls. For pausing a video in daily talk, people say 멈추다 or 일시 정지하다.

examples.en: The teacher enters the students in the contest.
I signed my child up for the camp.
I want to let my younger sibling join the game.
We plan to have every class take part in the event.
It costs money to enter a player.
I'm going to submit the form to enter the team.

explain: 다른 사람이 어떤 모임이나 대회에 들어가도록 해 줄 때 써요. 자기가 가는 건 '참가하다'예요. 이 단어는 맡긴 사람, 데려간 사람의 입장에서 말해요.

phrases.en: The teacher gets the students to take part in the discussion.
phrases.nuance_ko: '참가시키다'와 비슷하고 토론이나 활동에 더 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 참가시키다 but fits discussions and activities better.

phrases.en: The parents let their child take part in the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: '참가시키다'를 풀어서 쉽게 말한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy, spelled-out way of saying 참가시키다.

phrases.en: We don't let an injured player take part in the game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가를 넣지 않는다는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form meaning you do not let someone join.

explain_en: Used when you cause another person to join an event or contest. Going yourself uses the plain participation verb. This one speaks from the viewpoint of the person who arranges it.

examples.en: My eldest is starting university this year.
My eldest takes good care of her younger sibling.
I gave my eldest a little pocket money.
My older and younger kids fight often.

examples.ko: 큰애 학교 때문에 이사를 가기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to move because of my eldest's school.
I have to go to the school to pick up my eldest.

explain: 부모가 맏이 자녀를 말할 때 쓰고, 아들이든 딸이든 상관없어요. 짝말은 '작은애'이고, 형제가 셋 이상이면 '둘째', '막내'를 써요. '첫째'와 비슷하지만 '큰애'가 더 구어체예요.

phrases.en: My eldest child is a middle school student.
phrases.nuance_ko: '큰애'와 같은 뜻이고 조금 더 단정한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same as 'keunae' but a little neater in tone.

phrases.en: My first child is seven this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순서를 말하는 중립적인 표현이고 '둘째, 셋째'와 이어서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A neutral word about order, used with 'second, third'.

phrases.en: I'll try calling my eldest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족끼리 편하게 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in casual family talk.

explain_en: Parents use it for their eldest child, whether a son or a daughter. The counterpart is '작은애', and with three or more children you use '둘째' and '막내'. It is similar to '첫째' but more conversational.

examples.ko: 커피에 티스푼으로 설탕을 두 번 넣어요.
examples.en: I add sugar to my coffee with a teaspoon, twice.
Sorry, but could you give me one more teaspoon?

examples.ko: 카레 가루는 티스푼으로 한 번만 넣으세요.
examples.en: Add the curry powder with a teaspoon, just once.
The teaspoon is small, so it's inconvenient for eating soup.

examples.ko: 티스푼은 서랍 두 번째 칸에 있어요.
examples.en: The teaspoons are in the second drawer.
I scooped honey onto a teaspoon and put it in the tea.

explain: 작은 숟가락은 '티스푼' 말고 '찻숟가락'이라고도 해요. 한국 요리책에서 양을 말할 때는 '작은술'(티스푼 한 숟가락)과 '큰술'을 써요.

phrases.en: I added a little salt with a teaspoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으로'를 붙여 무엇으로 넣거나 젓는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '으로' says what tool you use to add or stir.

phrases.example: 차에 꿀을 넣을 때 찻숟가락을 써요.
phrases.en: I use a teaspoon when I put honey in tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 티스푼과 같은 뜻의 한국어 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A Korean word with the same meaning as 티스푼.

phrases.example: 레시피에 설탕 한 작은술이라고 쓰여 있어요.
phrases.en: The recipe says one teaspoon of sugar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리책에서 양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in recipes to give an amount.

explain_en: A small spoon can also be called '찻숟가락' instead of '티스푼'. In Korean recipes, amounts are written as '작은술' (one teaspoon) and '큰술' (one tablespoon).

examples.en: The researcher trains the computer.
The teacher makes the kids learn in a fun way.
We trained the AI with lots of photos.
If you force a child to study, they come to hate it.

examples.ko: 모델을 학습시키는 데 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes a long time to train a model.

examples.ko: 음성 인식 모델을 학습시킬 데이터를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for data to train a speech recognition model.

explain: '학습시키다'는 컴퓨터나 인공지능을 훈련하는 말로 많이 쓰고, 사람에게 쓰면 '억지로 공부하게 하는' 느낌이 있어요. 아이나 학생에게는 '가르치다'가 더 따뜻하고 자연스러워요. 동물을 연습시킬 때는 '훈련시키다'를 자주 써요.

phrases.en: The researcher trains the computer with lots of data.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인공지능을 훈련하는 상황에서 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most common when training artificial intelligence.

phrases.en: I'm training the program right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 하는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it is in progress now.

phrases.en: Please don't force your child to study too much.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람에게 쓰면 억지로 시킨다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used about people, it feels like forcing them to study.

explain_en: 학습시키다 is common for training computers or AI, and when used for people it can feel like forcing them to study. For children or students, 가르치다 sounds warmer and more natural. For training animals, 훈련시키다 is common.

dis.h: formal; also used for training machines

p.n: 공부시키다 is not natural for machines or AI.

en: to restore; to bring back to health

examples.en: Enough sleep restores your strength.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 죽이 아픈 아이의 기운을 회복시켰어요.
examples.en: The warm porridge restored the sick child's strength.

examples.ko: 충분히 쉬면 지친 몸을 회복시킬 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you rest enough, you can bring your tired body back to health.
It takes time to restore trust.
This is an exercise that helps with recovery.
The government is trying to revive the economy.

explain: '회복하다'는 스스로 좋아질 때, '회복시키다'는 누가 또는 무엇이 좋아지게 만들 때 써요. 건강, 체력, 신뢰, 경제처럼 원래 상태가 있는 것에 써요.

phrases.en: Good food restores your health.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 상태로 돌아가게 하는 대상을 넣어 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put in the thing being brought back to its original state.

phrases.en: An honest apology restores trust.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 사이의 믿음에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be used for trust between people.

phrases.en: Rest restores your energy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주다'를 붙이면 도움을 주는 느낌이 생겨요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '주다' gives a feeling of helping.

explain_en: 회복하다 is when something gets better by itself, while 회복시키다 is when a person or thing makes it get better. It goes with things that have an original state, such as health, strength, trust and the economy.
